subject: VPC backup custody, retention, and proof-of-delete request
messages:
From: Alex Chen <ops@medallionhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: VPC backups & proof of handback for departure

Hi Naomi,

We are evaluating Redwood Private for a PHI-handling deployment in us-west-2. A few quick questions from our compliance team about how backups and exports are handled when customer-controlled storage is used:

1) If we configure customer-controlled S3 for persistent state (DynamoDB exports, snapshots), are backups ever replicated outside the region by Redwood?
2) For on-request handback/terminate flows, what evidence do you provide that snapshots/exports were deleted? Do you provide manifests, checksums, or signed attestations?
3) What is the typical wall-clock for a full purge of customer snapshots and backups (including S3 lifecycle tombstones and DynamoDB PITR exports)? We need an SLO we can put into our policy.

We may require a deletion attestation (signed) and a manifest of file checksums for our auditors. Can you confirm whether that is possible and what the process looks like?

Can we schedule a 30 minute call today or tomorrow to walk through?

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Operations
Medallion Health

---
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <ops@medallionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: VPC backups & proof of handback for departure

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and a proposed next step below.

1) Regional replication: If you configure customer-controlled S3 (customer-owned bucket in us-west-2) Redwood will write exports/snapshots only to that bucket and will not replicate copies to other regions under normal operations. For Redwood-managed object store (when customers do not provide a bucket) we restrict storage to the tenant's configured region (us-west-2) and do not replicate outside the region unless you explicitly opt into cross-region DR (we document that option).

2) Proof of delete / evidence: We provide a multi-part handback artifact set on request:
  - Snapshot manifest (CSV) listing object keys, sizes, MD5 checksums
  - Signed deletion statement (PDF/TXT) with a timestamp and deletion token
  - Optional S3 server-side delete markers and lifecycle logs exported (redacted) if you ask for them

3) Purge timeline: Typical timelines are:
  - Tombstone/soft-delete propagation: within 4–24 hours after we kick the handback job (dependent on the number of objects).
  - Final storage reclamation (background GC, removal from physical media indexes): 48–96 hours.

If you need a contracted 24-hour final purge SLO we can discuss an SLA exception (operational cost and a short coordination window required).

Technical notes (brief):
  - DynamoDB exports/PITR: when exported to customer S3 we create export objects in the provided bucket. We do not keep separate copy in Redwood-managed buckets unless you subscribe to Redwood-managed backups for additional DR.
  - Streaming / KV caches: ephemeral, not persisted to long-term backups.
  - Encryption: all exported objects are encrypted at rest using your CMK (if configured) or Redwood-managed CMKs; deletion removes the object and associated KMS metadata.

Next steps: I attached a short handback checklist and a sample snapshot manifest for a small export to illustrate the artifact set we can produce. If you want the signed attestation we will prepare a draft statement and route it for signature. Can we do 11:30am PT today for a call?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: handback_checklist.pdf (overview), snapshot-manifest-20250630.csv (sample)

Subject: Re: Question: VPC backups & proof of handback for departure

Alex — quick technical addendum from the infra team:

- DynamoDB point-in-time recovery (PITR) exports are implemented as on-demand exports that write snapshot bundles into the target S3 prefix you own. Each bundle contains a manifest.json and a set of compressed SST-style files; the manifest includes object checksums (SHA256).

- For Kinesis/DLQ/stream exports we push to the same customer S3 and include an index file per export batch.

- When you request handback we run the following sequence:
  1) Quiesce writes to the tenant store and create final consistent snapshot exports.
  2) Produce and sign a snapshot manifest (CSV/JSON) listing objects + checksums.
  3) Issue deletion commands against the customer-provided S3 prefix and confirm delete markers.
  4) Run backend GC to remove tombstoned entries from our indexer and purge local caches.
  5) Produce a signed deletion-statement and provide the execution log (redacted).

- CMK note: If you use your own KMS key we will not retain plaintext access for any objects after deletion; keys remain under your control.

I attached a sample deletion statement that mirrors what we send for customers doing a full termination. If you need the signed version to be notarized or to include specific regulatory language (HIPAA/HITRUST), flag that now and Karthik will coordinate with legal.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample-deletion-statement.txt
